page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage resources include a 66 GB local SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this hardware configuration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the D8s_v3 delivers modest computational performance. Single-core processing is limited, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the weak and poor categories respectively. Multi-core performance is relatively stronger, achieving an average rating in stress-ng multi-core testing. Memory bandwidth is generally constrained, with uncached read speeds at 35.34 GB/sec and write speeds at 21.67 GB/sec. Database and web serving capabilities are also on the lower end, as evidenced by weak Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput. However, the server demonstrates average performance in lightweight LLM inference tasks using a 135M model, reaching 157.1 tokens/second for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8s_v3 offers a balanced resource profile suitable for workloads that require moderate memory capacity without demanding high-performance single-threaded compute. The inclusion of dedicated vCPUs and Premium Storage compatibility provides predictable resource allocation. This server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including light web serving, development environments, basic database operations, and moderate multi-threaded applications that do not require high memory bandwidth or advanced vector instructions.
